content.title: About
content.content: Cheese strudel is a pastry made from thin, flaky dough filled with a creamy cheese mixture, often enriched with raisins, candied peel or vanilla. The dough is crisp, while the filling is soft and mildly sweet.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The strudel tradition originated in Austria, but in Russia it is commonly prepared with cottage cheese.
The thin dough is made from flour, eggs, butter and a small amount of water, giving it great elasticity.
The cheese filling may include cottage cheese, cream cheese, and sometimes lemon zest for aroma.
Strudel is usually served warm, dusted with powdered sugar or drizzled with melted butter.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Cottage cheese provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The cheese filling supplies calcium important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Cottage cheese contains vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: When modest amounts of sugar are used, strudel can be more balanced in carbs than many sweet pastries.

items.title: Probiotics
items.content: If fermented cheese is used, it may contain beneficial bacteria for gut health.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The cheese filling contains lactose, which can cause discomfort for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Milk allergy
items.content: People allergic to milk or dairy products should avoid this pastry.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: The buttery dough makes the strudel energy‑dense, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Excessive sugar in the filling raises the glycemic index of the product.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve cheese strudel warm, sliced into portions. It can be dusted with powdered sugar, drizzled with melted butter, or accompanied by a berry sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the strudel in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, refrigerate up to 5 days or freeze for up to 2 months.
